The procedure returns a step only after both strong Wolfe inequalities have been checked. Finite budgets and domain exits may return failure even when a strong Wolfe step exists; no convergence claim follows from the procedure alone.

If $t$ satisfies the Wolfe conditions of [[def-wolfe-and-strong-wolfe-conditions]] with $0<c_1<c_2<1/2$, then its descent angle $\theta$ satisfies
$$
t\ge\frac{1-c_2}{L}\frac{\cos\theta\,\|g\|_2}{\|p\|_2}.
$$
This is convergence of gradient norms to zero; it does not assert convergence of $(x_k)$ or that a limit point is a minimizer.
